source.title: An analysis of training and generalization errors in shallow and deep networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical approximation guarantees for zero training error together with bounded generalization error, using constructions and error measures different from the claim versions’ empirical tests.
record.gate_note: The paper studies regression approximation on a torus, not random-label fitting or standard gradient training. Its theorems and illustrative examples concern constructed trigonometric polynomials and periodic-activation networks.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional approximation bounds for constructed periodic-activation networks and trigonometric polynomials. These results concern interpolation of continuous regression targets, and do not test any of V1–V8. In particular, interpolation with bounded approximation error does not establish V1's random-label versus natural-label comparison or V2's test-error trend under widening.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive parameter and approximation-error guarantees depending on data characteristics and target smoothness, including shallow and deep regularized constructions. They explicitly distinguish this approximation-theoretic analysis from explaining observed generalization, which would also require analyzing practical training algorithms.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses approximation-theory constructions and a regularization objective; it does not train networks with standard gradient methods or fit random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The bounds depend on data-point separation, target smoothness or approximation error, network degree, and—for periodic-activation networks—the activation approximation error.

fits_no_version.finding: Conditional constructions interpolate regression samples while bounding uniform approximation error; regularized minimizers have training and distance-dependent pointwise error bounds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For periodic regression targets with specified regularity and data separation, suitable trigonometric-polynomial or periodic-activation constructions can combine interpolation or small training residuals with controlled approximation error.

record.problems: The results are theoretical approximation guarantees, not empirical tests of gradient-trained models. They rely on target-function regularity and, for some constructions, Fourier information; they do not analyze random-label memorization or standard training algorithms.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1–3 show illustrative error plots for |cos x| and specified interpolation operators, but the supplied text gives no numeric values and those examples do not test any listed claim version; they are not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, chance accuracy on random labels, and coexistence under the same architecture and training recipe.
Held-out error as gradient-trained ReLU networks widen beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes to the training recipe.
Dropout effects on held-out classifier error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with measured generalization gaps and comparison with other measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical results can test a claim, but these theorems address a different proposition from the eight specified versions. Theorem 4.2 additionally extends regularized pointwise bounds to DAG networks; it also fits no listed version. Row states indicate inability to determine the specified claims, not a failure of the stated theorems.

versions.untested_parts: No fixed random labels, natural-label benchmark, or standard gradient training recipe is tested.
No network-width sweep beyond an interpolation threshold is tested.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison is tested.
No adaptive optimizer or SGD comparison is tested.
No sharpness or other measured property is compared with a generalization gap.
No training examples are removed or retraining comparison performed.
